reason: The pancreatic sensing cells sit beside glucose-rich blood and should initiate the after-meal response.

reaction: The separate branches make its targets clear.
reason: The liver contains glycogen and is a target of insulin, suggesting an after-meal storage response.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose storage as glycogen in the liver.

reaction: The distinction from muscle-style transporter insertion is useful.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the other target of the after-meal insulin signal.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose uptake by muscle, including through transporter insertion.

reaction: The weakening insulin signal makes the feedback clearer.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells can respond to the lower glucose level between meals.
expectation: The pancreas will release a signal, likely glucagon, that helps maintain blood glucose.

reaction: The contrast with the insulin response is clear.
reason: The liver's glycogen provides a plausible source of glucose between meals.
expectation: Glucagon will promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release from the liver into blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release, with the signal diminishing as glucose rises; both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback completes the contrast with the after-meal response clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing insulin's effects on liver and muscle was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish liver storage from increased muscle membrane transporters.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial insulin-release combination was straightforward and added less detail than following the hormone to its targets.

surprise.text: The liver picture explicitly distinguishes its glucose entry from muscle-style transporter insertion, a useful qualification to the shared insulin response.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each pairing followed a pictured signal or target.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrasting hormone pathways and feedback made the constructions informative, though the pairings were fairly predictable.
